questions.question_text: A vertical mast $OT$ is supported by two cables anchored at ground points $A$ and $B$. Cable $AT$ is $38\text{ m}$ long with an angle of elevation to the top $T$ of $47^{\circ}$. Anchor point $B$ is on horizontal ground $25\text{ m}$ from base $O$. What is the angle of elevation of $T$ from $B$, to the nearest degree?

options.why: Used $\cos 47^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin 47^{\circ}$ to find the height $OT$, calculating $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{38\cos 47^{\circ}}{25}\right) \approx 42^{\circ}$.
Inverted the tangent ratio as $\frac{25}{38\sin 47^{\circ}}$, calculating the complementary angle at the top of the mast.
Divided the slant cable length $38$ directly by $25$ rather than finding the vertical height $OT = 38\sin 47^{\circ}$ first.

questions.question_text: From point $P$ due south of a vertical tower $OT$ of height $90\text{ m}$, the angle of elevation of $T$ is $27^{\circ}$. From point $Q$ due east of the tower, the angle of elevation of $T$ is $38^{\circ}$. What is the distance $PQ$ across the ground, to the nearest metre?

options.why: Added the two ground distances $OP + OQ$ directly instead of applying Pythagoras' theorem $PQ = \sqrt{OP^2 + OQ^2}$.
Multiplied by tangents ($90\tan 27^{\circ}$ and $90\tan 38^{\circ}$) instead of dividing by tangents to find ground lengths.
Used the average of the angles ($32.5^{\circ}$) in a single triangle calculation.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOP\text{:}$
$OP = \frac{90}{\tan 27^{\circ}} = 176.633\dots\text{ m}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOQ\text{:}$
$OQ = \frac{90}{\tan 38^{\circ}} = 115.195\dots\text{ m}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta POQ\text{:}$
$PQ = \sqrt{176.633^{2} + 115.195^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{31199.3\dots + 13269.9\dots}$
$= 210.877\dots\text{ m}$
$= 211\text{ m}$

questions.question_text: A rectangular block has dimensions $10\text{ cm} \times 8\text{ cm} \times 6\text{ cm}$ (height $6\text{ cm}$). What is the angle that the space diagonal makes with the base plane, to the nearest degree?

options.why: Used the side edge length $10\text{ cm}$ instead of the base diagonal $\sqrt{10^2+8^2} = \sqrt{164}\text{ cm}$, calculating $\tan^{-1}(6/10) \approx 31^{\circ}$.
Used the width edge length $8\text{ cm}$ instead of the base diagonal, calculating $\tan^{-1}(6/8) \approx 37^{\circ}$.
Calculated $\sin^{-1}(6/\sqrt{164})$ using the base diagonal as hypotenuse rather than as adjacent side.

questions.question_text: A right pyramid has a square base of side length $18\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $15\text{ cm}$. Find the angle of inclination of a triangular side face to the base plane, to 1 decimal place.

options.why: Used the full base side $18\text{ cm}$ instead of the distance from centre to edge ($9\text{ cm}$), giving $\tan^{-1}(15/18) \approx 39.8^{\circ}$.
Used the half-diagonal $9\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$ to calculate slant edge angle instead of face inclination.
Inverted the tangent ratio, calculating $\tan^{-1}(9/15) = 30.96^{\circ} \approx 31.0^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Distance from base centre to face midpoint: } OM = \frac{18}{2} = 9\text{ cm}$
$\tan\theta = \frac{15}{9} = \frac{5}{3}$
$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)$
$= 59.036\dots^{\circ}$
$= 59.0^{\circ}$

questions.question_text: From a radio mast of height $60\text{ m}$, station $A$ is on a bearing of $070^{\circ}\text{T}$ with an angle of elevation of $31^{\circ}$, and station $B$ is on a bearing of $160^{\circ}\text{T}$ with an angle of elevation of $41^{\circ}$. Find the distance $AB$ between the stations, to the nearest metre.

options.why: Added the two horizontal ground distances $OA + OB = 99.9 + 69.0$ instead of using Pythagoras' theorem on the perpendicular bearings.
Subtracted $OB$ from $OA$ ($99.9 - 69.0 = 30.9$) or evaluated an incorrect cosine rule.
Multiplied $60\tan 31^{\circ}$ and $60\tan 41^{\circ}$ to get horizontal lengths before combining.

questions.question_text: From point $X$ due south of a flagpole, the angle of elevation of the top is $36^{\circ}$. From point $Y$ due east of the flagpole, the angle of elevation is $48^{\circ}$. If the distance between $X$ and $Y$ along level ground is $72\text{ m}$, find the height $h$ of the flagpole, to the nearest metre.

options.why: Formed the equation using tangents rather than cotangents, solving $h\sqrt{\tan^2 36^{\circ} + \tan^2 48^{\circ}} = 72$.
Averaged the two elevation angles to calculate $72\tan 42^{\circ}/2$.
Omitted the square root when solving for $h$, calculating $72 / (\cot^2 36^{\circ} + \cot^2 48^{\circ})$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta XFY\text{:}$
$FX = h\cot 36^{\circ}, \quad FY = h\cot 48^{\circ}$
$(h\cot 36^{\circ})^{2} + (h\cot 48^{\circ})^{2} = 72^{2}$
$h = \frac{72}{\sqrt{\cot^{2} 36^{\circ} + \cot^{2} 48^{\circ}}}$
$= \frac{72}{\sqrt{1.9021\dots + 0.8107\dots}}$
$= \frac{72}{\sqrt{2.7128\dots}}$
$= 43.715\dots\text{ m}$
$= 44\text{ m}$

questions.question_text: Two observers $A$ and $B$ are $100\text{ m}$ apart on level ground. A tower $OT$ is due north of $A$ and due west of $B$. The angle of elevation of $T$ from $A$ is $22^{\circ}$, and the bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $055^{\circ}\text{T}$. Find the height $h$ of the tower, to the nearest metre.

options.why: Used $100\sin 55^{\circ}$ instead of $100\cos 55^{\circ}$ to calculate the ground distance $OA$.
Multiplied $100\tan 22^{\circ} = 40.4\text{ m}$ without resolving the horizontal triangle $\Delta OAB$.
Found the base distance $OA = 100\cos 55^{\circ} \approx 57\text{ m}$ but forgot to multiply by $\tan 22^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Since }O\text{ is due north of }A\text{, }\angle OAB = 55^{\circ}\text{.}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta OAB\text{:}$
$OA = 100\cos 55^{\circ} = 57.3576\dots\text{ m}$
$\text{In vertical right-angled }\Delta TOA\text{:}$
$h = OA\tan 22^{\circ}$
$= 57.3576\dots \times \tan 22^{\circ}$
$= 23.174\dots\text{ m}$
$= 23\text{ m}$

questions.question_text: From a lighthouse $OT$ of height $100\text{ m}$, boat $X$ has bearing $040^{\circ}\text{T}$ with an angle of depression of $20^{\circ}$, and boat $Y$ has bearing $140^{\circ}\text{T}$ with an angle of depression of $14^{\circ}$. Calculate the distance $XY$ between the boats, to the nearest metre.

options.why: Added the two radial distances $OX + OY = 274.7 + 401.1 = 675.8\text{ m}$ directly.
Used $\cos 100^{\circ}$ as $+0.1736$ instead of $-0.1736$, subtracting the cosine term in the cosine rule.
Assumed the horizontal angle $\angle XOY$ was $90^{\circ}$ rather than $140^{\circ}-40^{\circ}=100^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle XOY = 140^{\circ} - 40^{\circ} = 100^{\circ}$
$OX = \frac{100}{\tan 20^{\circ}} = 274.7477\dots\text{ m}$
$OY = \frac{100}{\tan 14^{\circ}} = 401.0781\dots\text{ m}$
$\text{By the cosine rule in }\Delta XOY\text{:}$
$XY = \sqrt{OX^{2} + OY^{2} - 2(OX)(OY)\cos 100^{\circ}}$
$= \sqrt{75486.3 + 160863.6 - (-38269.4)}$
$= \sqrt{274619.3\dots}$
$= 524.037\dots\text{ m}$
$= 524\text{ m}$
